title: Our newest TPUs: 8tx and 8i Max, built for the agentic era
body: Our newest TPUs: 8tx and 8i Max, built for the agentic era Nov 09, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link We’ve expanded our eighth generation TPU portfolio with TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max, marking four new TPU systems in a single year. Amin Vahdat SVP and Chief Technologist, AI and Infrastructure Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Read AI-generated summary We’re expanding our eighth-generation TPU portfolio with the new TPU 8tx for secure, confidential inference and TPU 8i Max for massive context windows. These systems help you manage complex agentic workloads by providing specialized hardware for security, density, and reasoning. You can learn more about these additions and our latest software updates by watching our broadcast or visiting the Google Cloud website to explore our full infrastructure lineup. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. We are expanding our eighth-generation TPU portfolio with the new TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max systems. TPU 8tx provides hardware-level security for sensitive data, while TPU 8i Max handles massive context windows. These systems join TPU 8t and TPU 8i to offer specialized performance for every AI lifecycle stage. We are making TPUs more accessible by supporting PyTorch, open-source software, and automated tools for developers. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points We first designed TPUs more than a decade ago motivated by Google’s internal demands, including voice recognition and language translation. Eight generations of TPUs later, the use cases have exploded, covering: i) training and serving our own Gemini models, ii) agentic workloads, iii) delivering services to Google Cloud customers on our cloud infrastructure, and most recently, iv) allowing customers to deploy TPUs directly into their own data centers. TPUs are now a rapidly growing business with nearly 100 customers — including frontier labs, trading firms, retailers, universities, and more. At Google Cloud Next in April, we introduced two new specialized TPUs in the same generation — 8t for large-scale training and 8i for real-time reasoning. TPU 8t and 8i offer up to 2.7 times better training performance and 80% better inference price performance, respectively, versus our previous generation of TPUs. Today, we’re taking that a step further, expanding our eighth-generation TPU portfolio with two additional systems: TPU 8i Max for massive context windows and the highest compute density per rack, and TPU 8tx for secure and confidential inference. This is the first time we have introduced four TPU systems in a single year. Our expanded eighth-generation TPU portfolio: TPU 8t, TPU 8i, TPU 8tx, and TPU 8i Max. While we’ve always co-designed our TPUs in partnership with Google DeepMind, we’re now increasingly getting feedback from external organizations on their specific needs. With computing moving from human to agent scale, businesses are asking for accelerators that can reason across AI models’ massive context windows. In addition, some highly regulated customers are asking for specialized encryption capabilities for unique workloads. The new TPU systems we are announcing today address this new reality. Coupled with our recent PyTorch announcements , our aim is to make TPUs more easily accessible to every developer and Cloud customer. By combining modular custom silicon with an open and easy-to-use software stack, we can deliver new hardware and system configurations at the pace of the AI industry. Building the computer around the chip Today, we’re announcing two new TPU systems — and there’s an important difference between a new chip and a new system. Designing a new chip means laying out billions of microscopic transistors on a silicon wafer in a multi-year process bound by the laws of physics and a complex, long-duration manufacturing lifecycle. A system, on the other hand, is about how we bring together the compute, networking, and storage around the chip. This can include how they are packaged with the chips, to quickly meet emerging customer needs and research use cases. When we built our very first TPU more than a decade ago, we knew AI software would evolve much faster than silicon manufacturing ever could. So we made a foundational bet on system balance and modularity, architecting our TPUs as building blocks as part of our AI Hypercomputer , so engineers could rapidly adjust packaging, high-speed memory, optical networking, and security around them. That approach allows us to deliver specialized supercomputers in a matter of months rather than years. Specializing for secure, high-context AI Each system in our eighth-generation TPU portfolio targets a distinct part of the AI lifecycle. TPU 8t and TPU 8i established the baseline for this generation of chips: TPU 8t was designed to be a training powerhouse for massive foundation models with maximum “goodput” — or the useful intelligence delivered per watt of energy used. TPU 8i is the reasoning engine, designed to break the memory wall, cutting inter-chip communication delays by up to half. Now, as enterprises bring autonomous agents into production, we have created two new configurations of these foundational systems to solve two urgent new challenges: hardware-level data security and million-token context scale. TPU 8tx TPU 8tx, our third eighth-generation system, is optimized for secure and confidential inference and is also great for small-scale training. It’s built for regulated enterprises and governments running frontier or proprietary models and autonomous agents alongside their most sensitive data. Normally, data is encrypted when stored or sent over a network, but has to be unlocked in memory while a computer processes it. Built on the same silicon as TPU 8t and paired with 5th Generation AMD EPYC CPU hosts, TPU 8tx builds security directly into the hardware layer, keeping sensitive data and model weights protected and isolated even while in active use. And by adopting the same low-latency Boardfly network we created for real-time reasoning, TPU 8tx keeps multi-step agents moving, delivering up to 2x lower latency compared to TPU 8t with a near-zero performance penalty. Pairing training-grade compute with a fast inference network also means organizations can simultaneously run and customize their models on a single system. TPU 8tx enables teams to fine-tune models using their private data, distill large models into smaller ones, and train their agents through reinforcement learning, all without needing to migrate sensitive data between separate clusters. Designed for sensitive enterprise workloads, TPU 8tx provides hardware-level confidential compute for private fine-tuning and secure agent execution. TPU 8i Max Our fourth system, TPU 8i Max, is built for a different problem: the memory wall. When dozens of AI agents work together across an entire software codebase or hours of video at once, memory bandwidth quickly becomes the bottleneck. So we took two low-latency TPU 8i chips and combined them onto a single package. TPU 8i Max scales compute and memory in lockstep, delivering double the compute, double the SRAM and double the HBM bandwidth of TPU 8i, so processors remain equipped with essential data and so that large workloads do not stall. Further, because TPU 8i Max fits twice the silicon within the existing rack footprint, data centers can deploy significantly more computing power per square foot and per watt. The dual-chip TPU 8i Max system, engineered for massive context windows and maximum compute density. While flexible across workloads, together the four systems in our eighth-generation TPUs give customers a purpose-built accelerator for every stage of the agentic lifecycle. TPU 8t for scale-up training, TPU 8i for low-latency reasoning, TPU 8tx for confidential computing, and TPU 8i Max for massive context windows and the highest compute density per rack. Opening up TPUs to every developer When we launched the first TPU more than a decade ago, there were only a handful of companies running workloads that needed the processing power of a TPU. The use cases were specialized, so engineers would use optimized frameworks and hand-tuned code. Over the years, as AI has advanced, more and more companies began using accelerators. Now, AI adoption is at a point where TPUs are excellent for a wide range of companies and use cases, and as a result, we’ve been working systematically to remove barriers to adoption so that TPUs are as easy-to-use as general-purpose hardware. This investment comes together today across these key areas: Opening up TPU development to every PyTorch developer; no code rewrites needed: Last month, we open-sourced TorchTPU , so PyTorch code and Hugging Face models now run natively on TPUs, alongside out-of-the-box TPU backends for leading open-source inference engines like vLLM and SGLang. And to make hardware optimization effortless, our new open-source TPU agent suite (now in preview) plugs directly into coding tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and Google Antigravity to automate TPU onboarding in minutes, diagnose bottlenecks, and autotune custom kernels using plain language. For production deployments, our new open-source XLA Serving Engine lets you train models in Python and serve them directly in a low-latency C++ runtime across TPUs, GPUs, and CPUs. Industry-leading production performance on InferenceX and AgentX benchmarks: In production, what really matters is outcomes on real AI workloads rather than theoretical peak chip speeds. On industry-standard InferenceX and AgentX benchmarks , which test realistic agentic coding and long-context work, our native vLLM-TorchTPU software stack on TPUs achieved state-of-the-art price-performance marks. New evaluations demonstrate these advantages extend across a wide range of frontier open models and open-source serving stacks while maintaining high model accuracy. Upcoming software optimizations on this same hardware will drive those results even further. Eliminating idle compute waste for autonomous agents: Because AI agents are stateful, they frequently pause for seconds or hours while waiting on a database lookup, an external software tool, or human feedback. To make our agents more resource-efficient during those pauses, our new Agent Compute Engine software automatically suspends and resumes idle sessions, cutting operational infrastructure costs. Breaking through the memory wall with the model-state layer (TPU Sync): Building the computer around the chip also means unifying memory, storage, and networking in software. As agents reason across million-token contexts and continuous reinforcement learning (RL) loops, memory quickly becomes the bottleneck. We’re open-sourcing TPU Sync , the model-state layer for TPU clusters. TPU Sync turns chip HBM, host DRAM, shared storage, and the data center network into a single, co-designed memory hierarchy — automatically tiering massive KV caches off the chip in milliseconds, streaming context across disaggregated prefill and decode nodes, and synchronizing RL weights to cut KV transfer latency and Time to First Token (TTFT) by more than 90%. Scaling distributed workloads across TPUs from a single controller: Now generally available on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), Cloud Pathways brings the Google DeepMind runtime behind Gemini to every Google Cloud customer. Using a single-controller architecture and pathwaysutils , you can orchestrate large-scale TPU systems across multiple slices as if they were one local machine for pre-training, reinforcement learning, and multihost inference. Cloud Pathways keeps long-running jobs moving through hardware disruptions with colocated Python sidecars, sub-minute slice hot-swapping, and elastic resharding. Stitching custom TPU topologies on-demand with GKE dynamic slicing: Now generally available, GKE dynamic slicing decouples physical hardware provisioning from logical slice formation using optical circuit switching (OCS) technology. By dynamically assembling TPU cubes into larger topologies (super-slicing) or partitioning them into smaller, isolated workloads (sub-slicing) on-the-fly, this update completely eliminates rigid, manual nodepool recreation cycles. This topology agility slashes job startup times by up to 5x and accelerates fault recovery by up to 4.5x, maximizing overall fleet utilization and workload goodput across all TPUs. Co-designing with a decade of experience Shipping four TPU systems and a unified, open software stack in a single year only happens when silicon architects, networking engineers, compiler teams, and Google DeepMind researchers build side-by-side. Increasingly, we’re even tapping into AI to ideate and build the next generation of AI infrastructure. From using Google DeepMind’s AlphaChip reinforcement learning system to using Gemini to deliver chip layouts in hours rather than weeks, we’re using TPU-powered AI services to rapidly accelerate next-generation TPU hardware development. This is true co-design and a unique Google differentiator. Learn more about our new TPU systems by tuning into today’s broadcast at 9 a.m. PT. title: Merced County teacher indicted for distribution of child sexual abuse material (CSAM)
body: Press Release Merced County teacher indicted for distribution of child sexual abuse material (CSAM) Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of California FRESNO, Calif. — On Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026, a federal grand jury returned a two-count indictment against Patrick Silva, 38, of Hilmar, charging him with distribution of child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and possession of CSAM, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced. According to court documents, from November 2024 to September 2025, Silva used the internet to distribute CSAM. During the same period, Silva was a teacher at the Delhi High School in Merced. Homeland Security Investigations, the Central Valley Internet Crimes Against Children Taskforce, and the Merced County Sheriff’s Office conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Luke Baty is prosecuting the case. Silva pleaded not guilty today at his arraignment. He was arrested last Friday and remains in federal custody. A detention hearing is scheduled for Nov. 12, 2026. If convicted, Silva faces a maximum statutory penalty of 30 years in prison and a $250,000 fine. Any sentence, however, would be determined at the discretion of the court after consideration of any applicable statutory factors and the federal Sentencing Guidelines, which take into account a number of variables. The charges are only allegations; the defendant is presumed innocent until and unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the United States Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute those who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.usdoj.gov/psc. Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - California, Eastern

title: Justice Department Awards Jackson, Mississippi, more than $63M to Combat Violent Crime and Restore Law and Order Through Model Cities Initiative
body: Press Release Justice Department Awards Jackson, Mississippi, more than $63M to Combat Violent Crime and Restore Law and Order Through Model Cities Initiative Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Jackson Was Selected Out of Nearly 50 American Cities to Receive Federal Funding to Strengthen Law Enforcement and Enhance Public Safety. Today, the Justice Department awarded Jackson, Mississippi, more than $63 million through its Model Cities Initiative (MCI), a flagship effort to reduce violent crime, restore law and order, and strengthen public safety in communities across the country. “The Model Cities Initiative reflects the Trump Administration’s commitment to reducing crime across the country and ensuring the safety of every American,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “These cities are setting an example of proactive law enforcement that will strengthen the rule of law and improve public safety in their jurisdictions. As violent crime rates continue to fall to historic lows, the Department of Justice is redoubling our efforts to invest in local communities and keep American families safe.” “Jackson has made real progress against violent crime, and that progress deserves recognition,” said U.S. Marshals Service Director Gadyaces S. Serralta. “The officers working these cases know their city and understand the challenges ahead.  This investment gives them an opportunity to build on the work they’ve already done, with better tools to investigate violent crime and bring those responsible before the courts.  The goal is simple: give good officers every advantage against violent crime.” “This is a tremendous win for Jackson and Mississippi. I’m grateful to President Trump and Attorney General Blanche for partnering with us to make our capital city a safer place,” said Governor Tate Reeves of Mississippi. “Since day one, we’ve made enhancing public safety a top priority. We’ve invested in law enforcement, put more officers on the streets and held criminals accountable. This investment will provide additional resources to combat crime and help protect the people of this amazing city.” “With this significant investment, the Trump Administration is demonstrating a commitment to the people of Jackson to help reduce criminal activity, restore law and order, and positively impact the quality of life for Jacksonians,” said Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch. “We are proud to be a partner with the City of Jackson and all our local, state, and federal partners in this effort to make Mississippi’s capital city stronger, safer, and more secure. A strong Jackson means a strong Mississippi.” “This investment gives Jackson more resources to strengthen public safety and support the people who protect our city every day,” said Mayor John Horhn. “I thank the Department of Justice for its support and our congressional delegation and state leaders for helping us get here. Funding is essential, but making Jackson safer takes all of us — faith leaders, neighborhood associations, educators, businesses, and neighbors working together. We want every family to be able to raise their children, pursue opportunities, and enjoy life in Jackson without fear.” “True public safety requires us to address not only crime, but also the conditions that contribute to it. The MCI Grant provides an opportunity to strengthen our forensic capabilities, technology, and invest in the people who serve this community,” said Chief of Police Dr. RaShall M. Brackney. “These investments are essential to building a police department that is not only better equipped to investigate and prevent crime, but also better positioned to address the complex challenges that shaped public safety in Jackson.” Image of Attorney General Todd Blanche at the Model Cities Initiative in Jackson, Mississippi Image of $63 Million Check Awarded to City of Jackson Jackson, Mississippi, was selected in large part because of its substantial progress in reducing violent crime. The city has cut annual homicides by more than half, from 156 in 2021 to 75 in 2025. While these gains are significant, Jackson continues to face persistent challenges related to gun violence, investigative capacity, and public safety infrastructure. Through the Model Cities Initiative, the city seeks to build on its recent successes by strengthening law enforcement capabilities, expanding intelligence-driven investigations, and enhancing coordination among local, state, and federal public safety partners. Jackson's proposal includes transforming its existing Real-Time Command Center into a comprehensive Real-Time Public Safety Center, modernizing forensic and ballistic analysis capabilities, and establishing a specialized unit to integrate ballistic evidence and criminal intelligence with targeted enforcement strategies. The city also plans to deploy a Sky-to-Street Public Safety Network utilizing unmanned aircraft systems to improve situational awareness, accelerate emergency response, and support crime reduction efforts. Additional priorities include expanding law enforcement staffing, strengthening services for crime victims, and enhancing behavioral health and community reentry programs. Collectively, these investments are designed to reduce violent crime, improve investigative outcomes, and create a sustainable, coordinated framework for public safety in Jackson. The MCI takes a whole-of-city approach to public safety, bringing together law enforcement agencies, local government officials, and community partners to develop comprehensive strategies that address the unique public safety challenges facing their communities. The applications submitted by the four selected jurisdictions exemplified the innovative, forward-thinking approaches the Department sought through the initiative. While each jurisdiction faces unique public safety challenges and brings different priorities, resources, and starting points to the initiative, the Department is confident in the strength of their proposals and their commitment to achieving meaningful results. Despite differing approaches, all four jurisdictions demonstrated a shared determination to reduce violent crime and make their communities safer. Through the initiative, the Justice Department will work with each jurisdiction to finalize and implement its public safety plan. Funding will support a range of priorities, including hiring sworn and non-sworn law enforcement officers and other personnel to support enforcement, prosecution, and related public safety activities; adopting new and improved technology; purchasing or leasing equipment; enhancing forensic capabilities and capacity; and providing services to address mental health and substance use issues and reduce recidivism. The Justice Department announced the Model Cities Initiative in June 2026 to build on early successes in jurisdictions such as Memphis, Tennessee, and Washington, D.C., in reducing violence, crime, and disorder. The initiative directs nearly $300 million in federal resources toward comprehensive public safety strategies that strengthen law enforcement, improve coordination among public safety partners, and address the factors contributing to crime and recidivism. Through these investments, the Justice Department will work alongside local partners to implement sustainable public safety solutions and deliver measurable results. The four Model Cities will help advance the Administration’s efforts to reject the status quo of allowing crime and disorder to go unchecked and restore law, order, and safety to communities across the nation. Jacksonville, Florida; Baton Rouge, Louisiana; and St. Louis, Missouri, have additionally been selected to receive federal investments supporting innovative, comprehensive, locally driven strategies to combat crime and enhance coordination among federal, state, and local law enforcement partners. The specific departments funded are: Baton Rouge - East Baton Rouge Parish, Louisiana; Jackson - City of Jackson, Mississippi; Jacksonville - City of Jacksonville Sheriff’s Office; and St. Louis - City of St. Louis Police Department. Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Violent Crime Component Office of the Attorney General Press Release Number: 26-1334
retained_feed_body: Today, the Justice Department awarded Jackson, Mississippi, more than $63 million through its Model Cities Initiative (MCI), a flagship effort to reduce violent crime, restore law and order, and strengthen public safety in communities across the country.

title: Man Sentenced to 14 Years for Attempting to Coerce a 15-year-old to Engage in Prostitution
body: Press Release Man Sentenced to 14 Years for Attempting to Coerce a 15-year-old to Engage in Prostitution Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of California Kelly.Thornton@usdoj.gov SAN DIEGO – K’John Henry Sands II of Los Angeles was sentenced in federal court today to 168 months in prison for attempting to coerce a 15-year-old minor to engage in prostitution. Sands pleaded guilty on August 25, 2026, to one count of Attempted Coercion and Enticement of a Minor. According to his plea agreement, Sands also admitted to video recording the minor performing oral sex on him. As a part of his scheme, Sands instructed the minor regarding how much to charge for commercial sex dates, supplied the minor with condoms for the dates, and then collected the proceeds. Sands’ conduct came to the attention of the San Diego Human Trafficking Task Force when, on June 2, 2025, the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children sent information about an active MegaPersonals ad for what appeared to be a juvenile in the San Diego area. On June 3, 2025, investigators arranged a ruse commercial sex date and recovered the minor. Investigators then learned that the motel room in which the minor was staying had been rented by Sands. “Those who prey on vulnerable children should know that law enforcement will pursue justice relentlessly,” said U.S. Attorney Adam Gordon. “This sentence proves that combating the trafficking and exploitation of children remains an utmost priority at the California Department of Justice,” said California Attorney General Rob Bonta. “Crimes against children will never be tolerated in California, and together, we remain dedicated to holding perpetrators of child exploitation accountable. I am grateful for the hard work of my team in the San Diego Human Trafficking Task Force that made securing this prison sentence possible." “This case reflects the strength of the San Diego Human Trafficking Task Force and its partner agencies, whose swift, coordinated, and victim-centered response helped safeguard a vulnerable child and bring the offender to justice,” said Kevin Murphy, Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations San Diego. “HSI remains committed to working with our law enforcement and community partners to protect children and support survivors of trafficking.” In the government’s sentencing memo, prosecutors noted that the defendant was unconcerned with his victim’s age.“Mr. Sands’ intentions were clear: (The victim) was expected to make Mr. Sands money… It apparently did not matter that (she) was just 15 years old.” This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Derek Ko, with prior assistance from Assistant U.S. Attorney Lyndzie M. Carter. If you believe you or someone you know has been a victim of human trafficking, investigators ask that you contact the San Diego Human Trafficking Task Force at 1-888-373-7888 or text 233733. DEFENDANT Case Number 25cr03258-BJC K’John Henry Sands II                                    Age: 26                         Los Angeles, CA SUMMARY OF CHARGES Attempted Coercion and Enticement of a Minor, 18 U.S.C., Section 2422 Maximum penalty: Life imprisonment with a 10-year mandatory minimum; $250,000 fine INVESTIGATING AGENCIES San Diego Human Trafficking Task Force San Diego Sheriff’s Office Homeland Security Investigations The San Diego Human Trafficking Task Force is a cooperative effort involving the California Department of Justice, California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation, California Highway Patrol, Federal Bureau of Investigation, Homeland Security Investigations, National City Police Department, Naval Criminal Investigative Service, San Diego City Attorney’s Office, San Diego County District Attorney’s Office, San Diego County Probation Department, San Diego County Sheriff’s Department, Chula Vista Police Department, San Diego Police Department, Southwest Border High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area, and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of California. This case is the result of the ongoing efforts of the Special Victims Unit.  Formed in April 2025, the SVU is tasked with leading collaborations between federal and local law enforcement in the investigation and prosecution of cases involving sex trafficking and child exploitation, civil rights, and labor trafficking. The SVU oversees the Southern District of California liaisons to the San Diego Human Trafficking Task Force and Project Safe Childhood Contact Kelly Thornton, Director of Media Relations Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Human Trafficking Component USAO - California, Southern Press Release Number: CAS26-1109-Sands

Sands pleaded guilty on August 25, 2026, to one count of Attempted Coercion and Enticement of a Minor. According to his plea agreement, Sands also admitted to video recording the minor performing oral sex on him.

title: Justice Department Sues the City of Glendale, California for Violating Citizens’ Second Amendment Rights Through Unreasonable Fees and Processes for Legal Firearm Permitting
body: Press Release Justice Department Sues the City of Glendale, California for Violating Citizens’ Second Amendment Rights Through Unreasonable Fees and Processes for Legal Firearm Permitting Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Today, the United States Department of Justice sued the City of Glendale, California, for violating citizens’ fundamental rights under the Second Amendment by requiring unreasonable fees to obtain concealed carry permits. “The Department of Justice is committed to protecting law abiding citizens’ right to keep and bear arms under the Second Amendment,” said Acting Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights Jesus Osete. “The City of Glendale cannot impose unreasonable fees and unbridled discretion that undermines that core constitutional right.” “The right to bear arms is a fundamental right the Founding Fathers enshrined during our republic’s earliest years,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli for the Central District of California. “Exorbitant government fees that interfere with this right are abhorrent to our Constitution and our nation’s founding principles. This Justice Department will not stand by and watch our freedoms be eroded.” The Glendale Police Department (Glendale PD) administers a permitting regime with a total cost of an initial application for a concealed carry permit ranging from $1,971.00 to $2,106.00. The total cost for a renewal application, which citizens must complete every two years, is $1,271.00 to $1,406.00. These exorbitant amounts are a stark contrast to costs from the previous fiscal year when Glendale PD required only a $100 fee for first-time applicants and a $25 fee for renewals. Glendale PD also requires applicant reference interviews, psychological exams, interviews of the applicant, and a review of public statements including social media. Glendale PD does not publish any objective standards that they apply to these checks. It is well established that concealed carrying is a right. New York State Rifle & Pistol Ass’n, Inc. v. Bruen , 597 U.S. 1, 38 n. 9, 70 (2022). Glendale PD’s permitting fees are an unreasonable barrier to exercising that right, and its permitting regime lacks the “narrow, objective, and definite standards” which Bruen requires. Glendale PD’s policies and practices, therefore, violate the fundamental rights to keep and bear lawful firearms. The Second Amendment Section of the Civil Rights Division enforces the Second Amendment , the Police Pattern or Practice Act ( 34 U.S.C. § 12601 ), and Executive Order 14206 . If you are a current or prospective gun owner and believe that a state or local government has infringed your right to keep and bear arms, please submit a complaint through www.justice.gov/crt/second-amendment-section. Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Civil Rights Component Civil Rights Division Press Release Number: 26-1337

title: Justice Department Sues Lyft for Denying Rides to Passengers with Service Dogs, Wheelchairs
body: Press Release Justice Department Sues Lyft for Denying Rides to Passengers with Service Dogs, Wheelchairs Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Today, the Justice Department (Department) filed a lawsuit against Lyft Inc., for discriminating against passengers with disabilities, including those who use service animals and mobility devices such as stowable wheelchairs. Lyft provides an important transportation option for millions of people throughout the United States. The lawsuit seeks $53 million for individuals with disabilities who Lyft has discriminated against, and who have submitted complaints to Lyft or the Department. “Individuals with disabilities should be able to rely on rideshare services free of discrimination,” said Acting Assistant Attorney General Jesus A. Osete of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. “We intend to uphold the ADA’s promise that people with disabilities are entitled to equal access in every part of public life, including essential transportation services.” “Our purpose in the Department of Justice is often to fight for what’s right on behalf of those who can’t fight for themselves. And there are few areas where the fight is more important than in ensuring equal access to transportation services for all Americans,” said U.S Attorney Craig H. Missakian for the Northern District of California. “We take these allegations of misconduct seriously and, like our case against Uber for similar discriminatory conduct, we will devote all the resources necessary to make things right. The stakes are high and we owe those with disabilities nothing less.” The lawsuit, filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, alleges Lyft violated Title III of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (ADA), which prohibits private transportation companies, such as Lyft, from discriminating based on disability. The ADA requires Lyft to transport individuals with disabilities and their service animals, and to provide rides and assist riders with stowable wheelchairs and mobility devices. A service animal is a dog trained to perform a task related to a person’s disability. Under the ADA, emotional support dogs are not service animals because providing emotional support is not a task related to a person’s disability. The Department’s civil complaint alleges that Lyft and its drivers routinely refuse service to individuals with disabilities; impose impermissible surcharges by charging fees such as cancellation fees to riders whom Lyft has unlawfully denied service; and refuse to reasonably modify Lyft’s policies, practices, or procedures where necessary to avoid discriminating against riders with disabilities, including by denying individuals with mobility disabilities the option to sit in the front seat when needed. The lawsuit seeks a court order to force Lyft to stop discriminating against individuals with disabilities, to modify its policies to comply with the ADA, and to train its staff and drivers on the ADA.  In addition to the monetary damages to compensate aggrieved individuals subjected to Lyft’s discrimination, the lawsuit demands that Lyft pay a civil penalty to vindicate the public’s interest in eliminating disability discrimination. To learn more about the Civil Rights Division visit www.justice.gov/crt , and to report possible violations of federal civil rights laws go to www.civilrights.justice.gov . For more information on the ADA, please call the department’s toll-free ADA Information Line at 800-514-0301 (TTY 1-833-610-1264) or visit www.ada.gov . Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Civil Rights Component Civil Rights Division Press Release Number: 26-1338

title: Buffalo man sentenced for gun possession
body: Press Release Buffalo man sentenced for gun possession Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of New York BUFFALO, N.Y. – U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Nazir Binhuguley, 24, of Cheektowaga, NY, who was convicted of possession of a firearm in furtherance of drug trafficking, was sentenced to serve 60 months in prison by U.S. District Judge Richard J. Arcara. On May 6, 2025, law enforcement executed the search warrant at Binhuguley’s Trent Square apartment, which he utilized for his drug trafficking activities. During the search, investigators seized three firearms, ammunition, a high-capacity pistol magazine, drug paraphernalia, a quantity of suspected fentanyl, and approximately $2,165 in cash. This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Buffalo comprises agents and officers from Homeland Security Investigations, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives, the Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigations, Department of Homeland Security Enforcement and Removal Operations, Customs and Border Protection, the Drug Enforcement Administration, the U.S. Coast Guard Investigative Service, the U.S. Marshals Service, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, the U.S. Secret Service, and the Diplomatic Security Service, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Western District of New York. The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Michael J. Adler. The sentencing is the result of an investigation by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Allen D. Davis, II, the Buffalo Police Department, under the direction of Chief Erika Shields, and the Erie County Sheriff’s Office, under the direction of Sheriff John Garcia. # # # # Contact Barbara Burns 716-843-5817 Updated November 9, 2026 Topics Homeland Security Task Force Firearms Offenses Component USAO - New York, Western

title: Denver Man Sentenced To 89 Months After Pleading Guilty to Drug and Firearms Charges
body: Press Release Denver Man Sentenced To 89 Months After Pleading Guilty to Drug and Firearms Charges Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Colorado USACO.PublicAffairs@usdoj.gov DENVER – The United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Colorado announces that Christopher Epperson, 56, of Denver, was sentenced to 89 months in prison after pleading guilty to one count of possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine and one count of being a felon in possession of a firearm and ammunition. According to the plea agreement and facts established at sentencing, between July and August 2025, Epperson, who was at the time an eight-time convicted felon with prior convictions for burglary, aggravated robbery, domestic assault, attempted discharge of an illegal firearm, and felony menacing with a real/simulated weapon, and currently on federal supervised release for a prior felon in possession of firearm and ammunition conviction, was seen by law enforcement selling drugs to multiple people. On August 13, 2025, when law enforcement tried to stop Epperson, he ran from police and, while he was running, threw a bag he was carrying on his person. Law enforcement retrieved and searched the bag and found 54.7 grams of fentanyl, 13.55 grams of cocaine base, and 102.5 grams of methamphetamine. Law enforcement also found other drug dealing paraphernalia and $9,106 in cash. Epperson was ultimately arrested and his car was subsequently searched. Inside the car, law enforcement found a loaded firearm. As part of his plea, Epperson admitted to possessing the fentanyl, meth, and cocaine base with the intent to sell them for human consumption. Epperson also admitted he possessed the loaded firearm to further his drug-trafficking activities. “The sentencing of this repeat offender is another step in our ongoing efforts to safeguard Colorado communities,” said United States Attorney for the District of Colorado Peter McNeilly. “We are committed to putting violent drug dealers behind bars.” “Fentanyl, methamphetamine, and cocaine continue to be trafficked and distributed in our region, and these illegal drugs continue to destroy lives and ruin communities,” said Drug Enforcement Administration Rocky Mountain Field Division Special Agent in Charge Mark Putnam. “Our thanks to the U.S. Attorney’s Office, District of Colorado, and our other investigative partners in getting Epperson a lengthy sentence.” Senior United States District Judge William J. Martinez presided over the sentencing. The Drug Enforcement Administration and the Denver Police Department handled the investigation. Assistant United States Attorney Miles Robinson handled the prosecution. Case Number: 25-cr-245-WJM Contact USACO.PublicAffairs@usdoj.gov Updated November 9, 2026 Component USAO - Colorado

title: Panga Boat Pilots Sentenced in Maritime Smuggling Event that Killed Four in Homeland Security Task Force Case
body: Press Release Panga Boat Pilots Sentenced in Maritime Smuggling Event that Killed Four in Homeland Security Task Force Case Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of California Kelly.Thornton@usdoj.gov SAN DIEGO – Jesus Ivan Rodriguez Leyva and Julio Cesar Zuniga Luna, both Mexican nationals, were sentenced in federal court today to 70 months in prison for piloting a panga which overturned near Del Mar, California in May 2025, resulting in the deaths of two Mexican national adults and two minors, ages 14 and 10, from India. “Today’s sentences reflect the serious consequences of placing greed above human life,” said U.S, Attorney Adam Gordon. Panga with cracked engine held together by duct tape was recovered at the beach “This sentencing follows an extensive investigation and the coordinated efforts of the Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) San Diego Marine Task Force and our law enforcement partners to hold human smugglers accountable for the devastating consequences of their actions,” said Kevin Murphy, Special Agent in Charge of HSI San Diego. “This case underscores the critical role of our partnerships in responding to maritime smuggling events, conducting complex investigations, and pursuing those who endanger lives for financial gain.” “Human smuggling organizations continue to show a reckless disregard for human life,” said U.S. Border Patrol San Diego Sector Chief Patrol Agent Justin De La Torre. “This tragedy underscores the deadly consequences of maritime smuggling and our continued commitment, alongside our law enforcement partners, to hold those responsible accountable.” Rodriguez and Zuniga pleaded guilty on April 14, 2026, to two counts of attempted bringing in illegal aliens resulting in death as well as two counts of attempted bringing in illegal aliens for financial gain. In a related case, three load drivers pleaded guilty to conspiring with others to transport and move aliens within the United States. Plea documents outlined an overarching conspiracy in which individuals in Mexico recruited drivers to assist in smuggling aliens into the United States by meeting maritime vessels transporting illegal aliens upon their arrival into the United States, concealing them in vehicles, taking them to load houses, and then further transporting them to their intended destinations within the United States.  The load drivers coordinated with these Mexico-based co-conspirators as well as with co-conspirators in the United States. The load drivers have already been sentenced. Please see 25-cr-02056-BJC. According to Rodriguez’s and Zuniga’s plea agreements, each admitted that they “piloted” the vessel from Mexico into the United States on May 5, 2025, with 19 aliens aboard, including three minors; that the vessel had no running lights or radio; was overloaded with more passengers than the panga could safely hold; and that the aliens aboard were only given trash bags to cover their clothes and were not properly outfitted for the voyage. They further admitted that after the panga left Popotla, Mexico, the motor experienced issues and they were forced to return to their launch site where the motor was quickly repaired, and they set sail once again for the United States. According to the plea agreement, as the panga approached the beach in Del Mar, Rodriguez and Zuniga told the aliens to remove their life jackets to make it easier to exit the panga and run to waiting vehicles. Unfortunately, when the panga was approximately 200 yards from United States shores, the motor yet again failed and the vessel capsized in the surf. Onlookers watched and filmed the event as law enforcement was notified. Homeland Security Investigations San Diego Marine Task Force, the U.S. Coast Guard, local lifeguards, and U.S. Border Patrol initiated a joint search and rescue operation. Ultimately, four undocumented aliens were located on the beach and were transported for medical care and three more were found deceased on the scene, including one minor. On May 21, 2025, a human foot was found on the shoreline near Torrey Pines State Beach. A DNA test was conducted and it was determined to belong to a 10-year-old who had been on the panga, bringing the death toll to four. During today’s hearing, U.S. District Judge Benjamin J. Cheeks told one of the defendants: “This case is a tragedy all around …As a result of your actions, there are four people who are no longer here on this planet. Four people who are no longer here to hold their family members, who are no longer here to enjoy life, to breathe the air.” This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Jill Streja, Sean Van Demark, Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Danielle Hickman and former Assistant U.S. Attorney Edward Chang. DEFENDANTS Case Number 25cr2057-BJC Julio Cesar Zuniga Luna                                 Age: 32                                  Mexico Jesus Ivan Rodriguez Leyva                           Age: 28                                   Mexico SUMMARY OF CHARGES Attempted Bringing in Aliens Resulting in Death – Title 8, U.S.C., Sections 1324(a)(1)(A)(i), (v)(II), and (a)(1)(B)(iv) Maximum penalty: Death or Life in Prison and $250,000 fine Bringing in Aliens for Financial Gain – Title 8, U.S.C., Section 1324(a)(2)(B)(ii) Maximum penalty: Ten years in prison with a three-year mandatory minimum and $250,000 fine INVESTIGATING AGENCIES Homeland Security Investigations – Marine Task Force U.S. Border Patrol U.S. Customs and Border Protection – Air and Marine Operations United States Coast Guard San Diego Lifeguard Service San Diego County Medical Examiner’s Office Contact Kelly Thornton, Director of Media Relations Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Human Smuggling Component USAO - California, Southern Press Release Number: CAS26-1109-Rodriguez

title: North Carolina Man Indicted for Mailing Antisemitic Threats to Jewish Organizations and Secret Service Protectees in South Florida
body: Press Release North Carolina Man Indicted for Mailing Antisemitic Threats to Jewish Organizations and Secret Service Protectees in South Florida Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Florida MIAMI – A federal grand jury in the Southern District of Florida has returned an indictment against Brian Charles, 58, for allegedly mailing antisemitic letters threatening violence against Jewish organizations and individuals protected by the U.S. Secret Service. According to court records, Charles, who was staying in the Charlotte, North Carolina, area at the time of the alleged offense, was arrested and made his initial appearance before a U.S. Magistrate Judge in the Western District of North Carolina. Upon arrival in the Southern District of Florida, Charles was ordered detained by the court. In July 2026, Charles, allegedly mailed threatening letters to officers and executives of the Holocaust Memorial Miami Beach, the American Jewish Committee’s Palm Beach office, the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, as well as two Secret Service protectees. All of the letters were mailed to recipients in the Southern District of Florida. The letters contained identical antisemitic messages, including a graphic image and threats of violence against Jewish people. Charles is charged with mailing threatening communications. If convicted, he faces a maximum penalty of five years in federal prison. Acting U.S. Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas for the Southern District of Florida and Special Agent in Charge Brett Skiles of the FBI Miami Field Office made the announcement. FBI Miami is investigating the case, with assistance from the U.S. Secret Service.  Acting U.S. Attorney Lorenzo Klukas also thanked the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of North Carolina for their assistance on this matter. Assistant U.S. Attorney Edward N. Stamm is prosecuting the case. An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Southern District of Florida at www.sdfl.uscourts.gov or at http://pacer.sdfl.uscourts.gov , under case number 26-cr-20411. ### Contact Public Affairs Unit U.S. Attorney’s Office Southern District of Florida USAFLS.News@usdoj.gov Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Violent Crime Component USAO - Florida, Southern

title: United States Attorney's Office Files Civil Forfeiture Action to Recover Cryptocurrency Involved in Romance Fraud Schemes
body: Press Release United States Attorney's Office Files Civil Forfeiture Action to Recover Cryptocurrency Involved in Romance Fraud Schemes Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts Scammers targeted individuals on online dating sites and Facebook BOSTON – The United States Attorney’s Office has filed a civil forfeiture action to recover 456,602 USDT (Tether), alleged to be proceeds of romance fraud schemes targeting individuals in Massachusetts and elsewhere on online dating sites and Facebook. The cryptocurrency currently has an estimated value of approximately $456,602. As alleged in the complaint, after cultivating a relationship of trust online, victims were introduced to cryptocurrency and encouraged to make investments on fake cryptocurrency platforms. Although victims believed they were sending funds to a legitimate cryptocurrency investment platform and earning profits, in reality those funds were sent to unhosted cryptocurrency wallets (wallets not hosted on a cryptocurrency exchange). When the victim attempted to withdraw funds but could not, even after paying additional funds for so-called fees and taxes, they realized it was a scam. The scam proceeds were traced to two cryptocurrency wallets and the funds were seized by authorities. It is a violation of federal law to use wire communications as part of a scheme to defraud or to obtain money or property by means of false or fraudulent pretenses, and property traceable to such fraud is subject to forfeiture. It is also a violation of federal law to conduct a financial transaction knowing that the transaction is designed to conceal the nature, location, source, ownership, or control of criminal proceeds, and property involved in such transactions is subject to forfeiture. A civil forfeiture action allows third parties to assert claims to property, which must be resolved before the property can be forfeited to the United States and returned to victims. This is one of several civil forfeiture actions the U.S. Attorney’s Office has filed seeking to forfeit cryptocurrency traced to fraud schemes targeting Massachusetts victims. Members of the public who believe they are victims of a cybercrime. including cryptocurrency scams, tech support scams, investment scams and business email compromise fraud scams, should contact USAMA.CyberTip@usdoj.gov . United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Ted E. Docks, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation Boston Field Office made the announcement today. Assistant U.S. Attorney Carole E. Head, Chief of the Asset Recovery Unit is prosecuting the civil forfeiture action. The details contained in the civil forfeiture complaint are allegations. Updated November 9, 2026 Attachment Complaint for Forfeiture and Affidavit Topics Asset Forfeiture Cybercrime Component USAO - Massachusetts

title: Las Vegas Man Sentenced to Seven Years in Prison for Trafficking Methamphetamine and Fentanyl, and Money Laundering
body: Press Release Las Vegas Man Sentenced to Seven Years in Prison for Trafficking Methamphetamine and Fentanyl, and Money Laundering Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Nevada LAS VEGAS – A Las Vegas man was sentenced today by United States District Judge Cristina D. Silva to 84 months in prison to be followed by three years of supervised release for his role in a conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine and fentanyl, and to launder thousands of dollars of drug proceeds to Mexico. The government recommended a sentence of 84 months in prison. “Fentanyl is a weapon of mass destruction in our communities, and those who traffic it are dealing in pure death,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. “The defendant poured thousands of these lethal pills onto our streets with a callous disregard for human life, caring only about his bottom line. Every single ounce he distributed was a potential overdose and a shattered family. We will remain relentless and aggressive in hunting down anyone who pushes this poison into our neighborhoods, and we will ensure they spend a very long time behind federal bars.” “Methamphetamine and fentanyl continue to devastate American communities,” David Olesky, Special Agent in Charge of the Drug Enforcement Administration Los Angeles Field Division, which covers Nevada. “Traffickers exploit our neighborhoods for profit, but today’s sentencing serves as a reminder that drug crimes will be met with strict accountability and zero tolerance. The DEA remains committed to working with our HSTF partners to cut off drug flows and block the money laundering networks funding Mexican drug operations.” According to court documents, between June 2025 and January 14, 2026, Efrain Cabada-Martinez conspired with co-defendants Juan Carlos Cabada-Mendoza, Isaac Theojaris Tapia-Cabada, and others to distribute methamphetamine and fentanyl in Las Vegas. Additionally, Cabada-Martinez conspired with employees at a money services business in Las Vegas to send drug proceeds from Las Vegas to drug suppliers in Mexico. Cabada-Martinez pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to distribute a controlled substance and one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering. The DEA investigated this case. Assistant United States Attorney Joshua Brister prosecuted the case. This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of U.S. law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. ### Updated November 9, 2026 Topics Homeland Security Task Force Drug Trafficking Opioids Financial Fraud Component USAO - Nevada

The government recommended a sentence of 84 months in prison.

title: New Orleans Man Indicted for Violating Federal Controlled Substances Act
body: Press Release New Orleans Man Indicted for Violating Federal Controlled Substances Act Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Louisiana shane.jones@usdoj.gov NEW ORLEANS, LA – On October 16, 2026, DOMINICK CURRY ("CURRY") , age 41, of New Orleans, was charged in a recently unsealed indictment with possession with intent to distribute controlled substances, in violation of Title 21, United States Code, Sections 841(a)(1), 841(b)(1)(A), and 841(b)(1)(B), announced United States Attorney David I. Courcelle. According to court records, on September 3, 2026, CURRY possessed, with intent to distribute, 400 grams or more of a mixture and substance containing fentanyl; and more than 50 grams of a mixture and substance containing methamphetamine. If convicted of Count 1 of the indictment, possession with intent to distribute 400 grams or more of fentanyl, CURRY faces a minimum term of ten (10) years up to a maximum term of life imprisonment, a fine of up to $10,000,000, and at least five (5) years of supervised release. If convicted of Count 2 of the indictment, possession with intent to distribute 50 grams or more of methamphetamine, CURRY faces a minimum term of five (5) years up to a maximum term of forty (40) years imprisonment, a fine of up to $5,000,000, and at least four (4) years of supervised release.  He also faces payment of a $100 mandatory special assessment fee for each charged offense. U.S. Attorney Courcelle reiterated that the indictment is merely a charge and that the guilt of the defendant must be proven beyond a reasonable doubt. The case was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, and Firearms; New Orleans Police Department; and the Slidell Police Department.  It is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Paul J. Hubbell, I.V. of the Narcotics Unit. This case is part of Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN), a program bringing together all levels of law enforcement and the communities they serve to reduce violent crime and gun violence, and to make our neighborhoods safer for everyone. On May 26, 2021, the Department launched a violent crime reduction strategy strengthening PSN based on these core principles: fostering trust and legitimacy in our communities, supporting community-based organizations that help prevent violence from occurring in the first place, setting focused and strategic enforcement priorities, and measuring the results. For more information about Project Safe Neighborhoods, please visit Justice.gov/PSN . Contact Shane M. title: Homeland Security Task Force Investigation Leads to Indictment of Multiple Defendants in Fentanyl-Related Death Case
body: Press Release Homeland Security Task Force Investigation Leads to Indictment of Multiple Defendants in Fentanyl-Related Death Case Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Utah SALT LAKE CITY, Utah – A 15-count indictment has been unsealed charging multiple individuals for their alleged roles in an organized criminal enterprise involving several drug-trafficking offenses, including the distribution of fentanyl that resulted in the death of another person. Christopher Lee Washington, 53, of Millcreek, Utah; Natasha Annette Ashworth, 39, of Salt Lake City; Keisha Brewer-Case, 23, of West Valley City, Utah; Brittany Cuevas Caldwell, 38, of Salt Lake City; and Keith Jerome Lewis, 59, of Salt Lake City, were indicted by a federal grand jury on October 21, 2026, in the District of Utah. According to court documents, beginning on a date unknown, but not later than April 29, 2026, and continuing through at least August 27, 2026, in the District of Utah and elsewhere, all five defendants conspired to distribute four hundred grams or more of a substance containing fentanyl; five hundred grams or more of a mixture of a substance containing methamphetamine; and cocaine. As alleged in court documents, on June 23, 2026, Washington intentionally distributed fentanyl, which resulted in the death of another person. Additionally, according to court documents, as part of the investigation, on August 27, 2026, while executing a search warrant on Ashworth’s residence, agents recovered approximately 19 pounds of methamphetamine, a brick of cocaine weighing approximately one kilogram, and approximately 21 grams of fentanyl powder. Drugs seized during the execution of a search warrant on August 27, 2026. Washington, Ashworth, Brewer-Case, Caldwell, and Lewis are charged with conspiracy to distribute fentanyl, conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine, and conspiracy to distribute cocaine. Washington is also charged with distribution of fentanyl resulting in death. Additional charges pertaining to the individual defendants are detailed in the indictment. Initial appearances have occurred or are scheduled throughout November 2026 before U.S. Magistrate Judge Daphne A. Oberg at the Orrin G. Hatch United States Courthouse in downtown Salt Lake City. United States Attorney Melissa Holyoak of the District of Utah made the announcement. The case is being investigated jointly by the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), Salt Lake City Police Department, and Unified Police Department of Greater Salt Lake. Assistant United States Attorney Vernon G. Stejskal of the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Utah is prosecuting the case. This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Salt Lake comprises agents and officers from Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), and the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Utah. An indictment is merely an allegation and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Updated November 9, 2026 Topics Homeland Security Task Force Project Safe Neighborhoods Components Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) USAO - Utah Press Release Number: 26-119

title: NVIDIA Announces New Planned Investments in Korean Startups at the MSIT-NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum
body: NVIDIA Announces New Planned Investments in Korean Startups at the MSIT-NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum November 9, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT and NVIDIA hosted the MSIT -NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum at COEX. Ryu Je-myung, vice minister of science and ICT , joined NVIDIA leaders to meet with over 20 Korean startups across foundation models, physical AI, AI infrastructure and AI semiconductors. NVIDIA also announced an investment in Korean startup Point2 , with additional investments planned in Motif Technologies , RLWRLD and Upstage. Point2 Technology, an AI interconnect company, builds scalable, radio frequency-based interconnects that move data between chips and racks in AI factories, offering an innovative alternative to conventional copper and optical interconnect solutions for AI cluster scale-up, delivering the reach, performance and efficiency needed for next-generation AI infrastructure. Motif Technologies , a Seoul-based AI lab, develops foundation models for building AI agents that carry out complex tasks, including Motif-3, a large language model released with open weights. RLWRLD, a physical AI startup based in San Francisco, Seoul and Tokyo, develops robotics foundation models that enable humanoid and industrial robots to perform complex real-world tasks that require five-finger dexterity, such as precisely inserting components, threading nuts onto bolts and kitting parts from moving conveyors. Upstage , a Korean enterprise AI company, develops Solar language models and document AI tools that help businesses extract information from complex documents, streamline workflows and build AI applications for everyday operations. The companies represent work across the full AI stack , from infrastructure to models to robotics applications. The planned investments build on NVIDIA’s work with Korea’s startup and venture community, including more than 1,000 Korea-based members of NVIDIA Inception , a program that helps startups grow with access to preferred pricing, technical expertise and opportunities for investor introductions. title: Korea Advances Physical AI Across Industries With NVIDIA
body: Korea Advances Physical AI Across Industries With NVIDIA November 8, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Tapping into the country’s strengths in manufacturing and engineering, NVIDIA is helping advance Korea’s physical AI ecosystem. The country’s industry leaders are applying accelerated computing, AI and simulation to everything from semiconductor manufacturing to robotics and autonomous vehicles. These efforts are helping bring physical AI from development into real-world production. Samsung Advances Semiconductor Engineering With Accelerated Computing and AI Physics Samsung Electronics is expanding its collaboration with NVIDIA to advance semiconductor innovation through accelerated computing and AI physics. The work spans materials research, process development and device engineering. In technology computer-aided design, Samsung is working with NVIDIA cuISS and NVIDIA cuDSS to accelerate computations involving sparse linear systems. The collaboration also extends to GPU acceleration for process and optical simulations. In materials research, Samsung’s sMOL platform has run selected quantum chemical calculations up to 5x faster end to end with NVIDIA cuEST . Samsung is also exploring NVIDIA cuEquivariance to speed up tensor operations used in training and inference for atomistic AI models. Samsung is developing chip-scale thermal and mechanical analysis workflows with NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo . In one AI homogenization case, combining AI-predicted effective material properties, coarser grids and GPU acceleration resulted in a roughly 1,600x speedup. Simulation time fell from about 18 hours for a fine-grid solve on a 32-core CPU to 41 seconds for a GPU-accelerated coarse-grid solve. Looking ahead, NVIDIA Agent Toolkit could connect these simulation tools and AI models, helping future engineering agents run analyses and compare design options. Kakao Mobility Collaborates With NVIDIA to Advance Autonomous Driving Development Kakao Mobility plans to build on NVIDIA’s autonomous vehicle computing and safety technologies to advance development of a level 4 autonomous driving system. The work combines Kakao Mobility’s proprietary driving software and experience operating in Seoul’s Gangnam district with NVIDIA’s vehicle computing platform. Kakao Mobility plans to use NVIDIA Hyperion , a reference platform for vehicle sensors and compute, powered by NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor. It also plans to use NVIDIA Halos to support safety across the development and validation of its autonomous driving technology. Initial development is planned around Kia purpose-built vehicles, integrating Kakao Mobility’s autonomous driving software with NVIDIA technologies. The effort aims to support future level 4 mobility services in Korea. LG Electronics Advances Robot Learning and Factory Simulation NVIDIA and LG Electronics successfully demonstrated NVIDIA Isaac GR00T-powered robotic manipulation and manufacturing tasks using LG’s CLOiD robot in an actual manufacturing environment. The collaboration implemented a physical AI data flywheel connecting real-world data collection, NVIDIA Cosmos-based data augmentation, GR00T model training, NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor onboard computing and simulation-based evaluation, establishing reusable workflows for continued development and validation of CLOiD’s robotic capabilities. The teams are using this work to refine a repeatable process for training, evaluating and improving robots for manufacturing. title: Korea’s AI Ecosystem Advances and Secures Agentic AI With NVIDIA
body: Korea’s AI Ecosystem Advances and Secures Agentic AI With NVIDIA Hyundai Motor Group and AIM Intelligence explore NVIDIA NemoClaw and OpenShell for secure enterprise agents, and LG AI Research opens API for ‘K-EXAONE-2.5’ trained on Nemotron datasets. November 8, 2026 by Nicola Sessions 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! As AI agents take on more work, they need capable open models and security that advances alongside them. Hyundai Motor Group is exploring NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints and the NVIDIA OpenShell runtime, while AIM Intelligence is integrating its Starfort platform with NVIDIA OpenShell to support secure AI agents for employee productivity and enterprise workflows . A key component of the NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform, OpenShell provides a secure runtime with sandboxed execution and policy-based controls to safeguard sensitive data, manage access to enterprise tools and govern autonomous agent actions. AIM Intelligence , a Korean AI security company, is integrating its Starfort agent control platform with NVIDIA OpenShell. The goal is to combine OpenShell’s runtime access controls with Starfort’s detection of malicious instructions and data leakage. The company is also considering a preliminary proof of concept for the public energy sector, with potential applications across enterprise, industrial and robotics environments. On the model side, LG AI Research is opening application programming interface access for K-EXAONE-2.5, developed using NVIDIA Nemotron datasets, including Nemotron-Personas-Korea . Nemotron-Personas-Korea is an open dataset of 7 million fully synthetic Korean personas, grounded in official Korean statistics, that model builders use to ground training data and evaluation in Korean contexts. NVIDIA Nemotron is a family of open models, datasets and techniques that help developers build specialized, efficient AI agents. Learn more about NVIDIA Nemotron open models and get started building secure agents with NVIDIA OpenShell . title: From Chips to Skills, NVIDIA and Korea Expand Sovereign AI Collaboration
body: From Chips to Skills, NVIDIA and Korea Expand Sovereign AI Collaboration November 8, 2026 by Jesse Clayton 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA and Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) are expanding their collaboration across the country’s sovereign AI ecosystem, from AI semiconductors and data center infrastructure to talent, startups, models, agents and security. The collaboration lays the groundwork for Korean NPU and XPU companies to explore participation in the NVIDIA NVLink Fusion ecosystem, and includes NVIDIA training and certification programs, hackathons and technical seminars to strengthen GPU utilization. Through Korea’s AI for All initiative, NVIDIA will collaborate with three selected consortia and four leading Korean foundation model builders, using NVIDIA Dynamo software to optimize and scale AI inference. In addition, NVIDIA today announced a collaboration with SK Telecom and Rebellions, supported by MSIT, to advance sovereign AI infrastructure for Korean models and workloads with NVIDIA NVLink Fusion. Read more in the press release . title: NVIDIA Dynamo Recipes Bring Korea’s Leading Open Models to Production
body: NVIDIA Dynamo Recipes Bring Korea’s Leading Open Models to Production November 8, 2026 by Amr Elmeleegy 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA is releasing Dynamo-optimized deployment recipes for Korea’s leading open models: A.X K2 from SK Telecom , K-EXAONE 2.0 from LG AI Research , Solar Open 2 from Upstage and Motif-3 from Motif Technologies . As models grow beyond the capacity of a single GPU, they must be split across multiple GPUs, requiring careful coordination of request routing and communication to maintain performance. NVIDIA Dynamo is an open source, distributed inference-serving framework built to deploy models in multi-node environments at data center scale. It handles this routing and communication to maximize inference performance. Optimized for NVIDIA B200 GPUs, these recipes take the guesswork out of deployment, delivering up to 2x performance out of the box. They help developers bring Korea’s open models into production faster and turn them into broadly accessible AI for All services. Learn more about NVIDIA Dynamo .
